claims: Every validated XRPL transaction destroys a small amount of XRP as its transaction cost; the fee is not paid to a validator or other party.
The documented minimum standard transaction cost is 10 drops, or 0.00001 XRP, before load scaling.
The fee can rise with network load and the base fee can change through validator fee voting.
USDC transfers on XRPL therefore require an XRP-denominated network fee, even when the transferred asset is USDC.
analytical_implications: Stablecoin activity on XRPL creates a mechanical XRP fee sink, but the base fee is tiny and is not proportional to transferred dollar value.
XRPL DEX auto-bridging may use XRP as a bridge asset when routing chooses that path; this is conditional and not true of every USDC transfer.
One million standard transactions at the unscaled 10-drop minimum would destroy 10 XRP; this is an illustrative calculation, not an observed USDC transaction count.
limitations: No current USDC-specific XRPL transaction count or DEX auto-bridge routing share was retrieved in this run.
Do not convert network fee mechanics into a material price-demand claim without volume and fee history.
